moduleTitle: Managing Case relationships for the Business Architect
learningObjectives: Describe the role of the parent and child Case relationship for managing workflow complexity.
Explain the business value in creating child Cases.
Identify the context for using Wait steps to manage Case dependencies.
Explain how the search duplicate Case logic identifies duplicate Cases.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Creating Case Relationships (Parent and Child Cases)

elements.description: A parent/child hierarchy decomposes complex work into independently processed Cases. Configure the parent’s dependency on the required child outcomes; creating children alone does not establish every waiting rule.

Child Cases break a large, complex workflow into smaller, manageable, reusable units that can run in PARALLEL, be owned by different teams, carry their own data/SLAs, and be reused across applications — reducing complexity and improving operational efficiency.

elements.text: A parent Case is the general contractor; child Cases are the specialized subcontractors (plumbing, electrical) working in parallel. The contractor coordinates them and finishes once their work is done.

elements.description: Create Case can copy selected parent values into the child as a snapshot at creation. If the child must follow later parent changes, configure a reference instead; copying does not create ongoing synchronization.

bulletPoints: Parent/child relationships manage workflow COMPLEXITY by decomposing work into modular Case Types.
Child Cases enable parallelism, specialization, independent ownership/SLAs, and reuse.
A child Case can be created automatically (an automation that creates a Case) within the parent's flow.

elements.description: A Wait Step PAUSES a Case until a defined condition is met, which is how you manage dependencies between Cases (e.g., a parent waiting on its child Cases) or time-based pauses.

Case Dependency pauses for any or all children of a configured type to reach a specified status. To be resolved accepts statuses beginning Resolved, including rejected/duplicate outcomes; it is not the same as requiring successful completion. Timer waits for a duration or reference timestamp.

elements.text: A Wait Step is a relay handoff: the parent runner pauses at the line until the child runners finish their legs (case dependency) or until the official's clock hits a set time (timer), then continues.

bulletPoints: Children must already exist in the hierarchy before Wait; otherwise no dependencies exist and Wait is skipped.
Choose any/all, target type/status and current-versus-subsequent-status behavior deliberately.
For an enforced dependency, do not enable user cancellation that bypasses the required wait.
Timer date calculation, business calendars and user-assignment delays are separate from Case Dependency.

elements.description: A user might create a Case with the same data values as an existing Case (e.g., same customer, request date, items). Identifying and resolving duplicates saves time and money, so it is important to know how Pega detects them.

Pega provides the Search duplicate Cases Process, implemented as a Search duplicate Cases Step. When a Case enters the Step, the system uses BASIC conditions and WEIGHTED conditions to compare specific property values against Cases already in the system.
Two ways to configure duplicate Case search conditions:
items: BASIC — conditions MUST match (mandatory; all must be true)
WEIGHTED — each condition carries a numeric score; the SUM must reach a configured threshold (more flexible)

elements.description: When a user decides the current Case is a duplicate, they resolve it with a Resolved-Duplicate status and processing ends; the flow can be customized to let the user open the original Case to make updates.

elements.text: Duplicate detection is airport security: basic conditions are the mandatory ID check (must pass), and weighted conditions are points on a watchlist — once your points cross the threshold, you're pulled aside as a likely match.

bulletPoints: Example: DOB basic match plus four weighted matches at 25 each yields 100 against threshold 50: potential duplicate, requiring review.
Resolved-Duplicate ends processing; the user continues with the original Case.

examPitfalls.title: Why use child Cases
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Child Cases exist to manage complexity through modular, parallel, reusable Case Types — not merely to add layers.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Decompose complex work into child Cases for parallelism, specialization, independent SLAs, and reuse.

examPitfalls.title: Wait Step: dependency vs. timer
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The two Wait types are swapped: case-dependency (wait for other/child Cases to reach a status) vs. timer (wait until a date/time).
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Waiting on child Cases → case-dependency Wait; waiting until a date/time → timer Wait.

examPitfalls.title: Basic vs. weighted conditions
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Basic conditions MUST match; weighted conditions accumulate toward a threshold. Candidates conflate the two.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Mandatory match = basic; scored match summed against a threshold = weighted.

examPitfalls.title: Threshold logic
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A Case is flagged only when basic conditions match AND the summed weighted value meets/exceeds the threshold.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Add the matching weighted condition values; compare to the threshold (e.g., 100 ≥ 50 → duplicate).

examPitfalls.title: Resolved-Duplicate status
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The specific resolution status for a confirmed duplicate is Resolved-Duplicate, after which processing ends.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Confirmed duplicate → resolve as Resolved-Duplicate; optionally open the original Case to update it.

examPitfalls.title: Search duplicate Cases is a Step/Process
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Duplicate detection is implemented as the Search duplicate Cases Step (from the Search duplicate Cases Process) in the Life Cycle.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: When a question asks how duplicates are detected, the answer is the Search duplicate Cases Step using basic + weighted conditions.

examPitfalls.title: Parent waits for children
examPitfalls.trapDescription: To make a parent depend on child completion, use a Wait Step configured for case dependency — not an SLA.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Create children before Wait; choose all/any and required status, and disable user cancellation for a strict dependency.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A complex claims workflow is decomposed so that investigation, payment, and document collection each run as their own focused Case Type contributing to the overall claim. What relationship is being used?

options.text: Parent and child Case relationships
A single monolithic Case Type
A Work Queue hierarchy
A Ruleset stack

practiceQuiz.hint: Parent/child Case relationships decompose complex work into modular Case Types that collaborate.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Focused child Cases contribute to a parent outcome. Configure any required waiting explicitly; hierarchy alone does not define the whole dependency policy.

optionExplanations.A: Focused child cases contribute to the parent's overall outcome.
optionExplanations.B: A monolithic case does not provide the separate case types requested.
optionExplanations.C: Queues allocate work rather than define this case hierarchy.
optionExplanations.D: Ruleset ordering does not create parent-child case relationships.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is recommending a child Case architecture to a client managing a complex multi-party insurance Claims process. Which TWO are key business benefits of creating child Cases?

options.text: Work can run in parallel and be owned by different teams with their own SLAs
Complex workflows are broken into modular, reusable units
They eliminate the need for any data
They remove the parent Case entirely

practiceQuiz.hint: Child Cases enable parallel, independent work streams and reusable sub-processes across Case Types.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Child Cases enable parallel, independently-owned work with separate SLAs and decompose complex processes into reusable, focused units. They do not eliminate data from the parent Case or remove the parent's oversight. No partial credit.

optionExplanations.A: Independent cases support separate owners and service-level policies.
optionExplanations.B: Focused case types reduce monolithic workflow complexity.
optionExplanations.C: Child work still needs data to complete its outcome.
optionExplanations.D: The parent coordinates the overall outcome rather than disappear.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A parent Case must NOT advance until all of its child Cases are resolved. Which configuration achieves this?

options.text: A Case Dependency Wait for all already-created required children to be resolved, without user cancellation
An SLA deadline on the parent
Routing the parent to a Work Queue
A duplicate Case search

practiceQuiz.hint: Any is not All, and resolved is not necessarily successfully completed.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Create the children before Wait, choose all required child dependencies and prevent user cancellation if the requirement is strict. To be resolved includes any Resolved-prefixed status; require a specific success status if rejection must block progress.

optionExplanations.A: Waiting for all existing children to resolve enforces the dependency.
optionExplanations.B: A deadline schedules escalation rather than wait for child resolution.
optionExplanations.C: Queue placement does not enforce a child-status dependency.
optionExplanations.D: Duplicate detection does not wait for child completion.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Case must pause until the first business day of next month before continuing. Which Wait Step type fits?

options.text: A timer Wait (wait until a specific date/time)
A case-dependency Wait
A cascading approval
A Decision Table

practiceQuiz.hint: A timer Wait Step pauses the Case until a specific date and time arrives, not until another Case resolves.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A timer pauses until the configured timestamp. Calculate the first-business-day date according to the relevant calendar; the wait type itself does not infer that business date.

optionExplanations.A: A timer can wait until the configured reference timestamp.
optionExplanations.B: Dependency waiting responds to case status rather than this date.
optionExplanations.C: Ordered approval is not a time-based pause.
optionExplanations.D: A table selects a result rather than schedule continuation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the Search duplicate Cases Step, which condition type MUST match for a Case to be considered a potential duplicate?

options.text: A basic condition
A weighted condition
An SLA condition
An Access Role condition

practiceQuiz.hint: Basic conditions must ALL match (mandatory); weighted conditions accumulate a score toward a threshold.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Basic conditions are mandatory — all must match for a duplicate to be flagged. Weighted conditions accumulate scores that must reach a threshold but are not individually mandatory. The other options are not part of duplicate-detection logic.

optionExplanations.A: The basic condition is the required candidate match.
optionExplanations.B: Weighted matches contribute a score after required criteria.
optionExplanations.C: Service levels do not define duplicate identity matching.
optionExplanations.D: Permissions do not define the duplicate search's basic criterion.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A duplicate search uses date of birth as a basic condition and four weighted conditions worth 25 each, with a threshold of 50. A new Case matches the DOB and all four weighted conditions. What happens?

options.text: It is flagged a potential duplicate (basic matches and 100 ≥ 50 threshold)
It is ignored because weighted conditions never matter
It is auto-deleted
It is flagged only if the threshold were 200

practiceQuiz.hint: Weighted conditions add up their scores and the total must cross the configured threshold value.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The basic condition (DOB) matches and the weighted total is 4×25=100, which meets/exceeds the threshold of 50, so the Case is flagged as a potential duplicate.

optionExplanations.A: The required match and score satisfy this example's duplicate criteria.
optionExplanations.B: Weighted matches contribute to the configured threshold.
optionExplanations.C: A candidate requires a decision rather than automatic deletion.
optionExplanations.D: A threshold of two hundred would exceed this score.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A user confirms a Case is a duplicate. How is it resolved?

options.text: Resolve it with a Resolved-Duplicate status, ending processing
Delete the original Case
Route it to a Work Queue indefinitely
Increase its SLA urgency

practiceQuiz.hint: A confirmed duplicate uses Resolved-Duplicate; this is not a child-completion question.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A confirmed duplicate is resolved as Resolved-Duplicate and processing ends; the flow can be customized so the user opens the original Case to update it.

optionExplanations.A: The duplicate status ends the redundant case's processing.
optionExplanations.B: The original should remain available for the valid work.
optionExplanations.C: Indefinite queueing preserves unnecessary duplicate work.
optionExplanations.D: Higher priority does not resolve duplication.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How does the Search duplicate Cases Step compare a new Case to existing ones?

options.text: By evaluating basic conditions (must match) and weighted conditions (summed against a threshold)
By comparing only the Case ID
By checking the Ruleset version
By routing to the customer for review

practiceQuiz.hint: A Search duplicate Cases Step uses two condition types: mandatory basic conditions and scored weighted conditions.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Step uses basic conditions (mandatory matches) plus weighted conditions whose matching weights are summed and compared to a threshold. Case ID/Ruleset checks aren't the mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: Required matches and scored matches serve different parts of the search.
optionExplanations.B: A new case's distinct ID does not identify duplicate business requests.
optionExplanations.C: Ruleset revisions do not describe duplicate business data.
optionExplanations.D: Candidate matching is a configured search rather than customer routing.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is reviewing a proposed Case architecture where one parent Case will spawn multiple independently-managed child Cases. Which statement about parent/child Case design is correct?

options.text: Child Cases are focused, modular Case Types that can run in parallel and contribute to the parent's outcome
A parent Case can never spawn more than one child
Child Cases must always be created manually by the customer
Parent and child Cases must share a single Worklist item

practiceQuiz.hint: Child Cases are modular, can run in parallel, and contribute their resolved outcomes back to the parent Case.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Child Cases are focused, modular Case Types (one or many) that can run in parallel and feed the parent's outcome. The other statements are false.

optionExplanations.A: Independent child work supports a modular overall outcome.
optionExplanations.B: Multiple children can contribute to one parent.
optionExplanations.C: A Create Case automation can create child cases.
optionExplanations.D: Separate child workflows can have their own assignments.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is designing a mortgage approval Case that has separate child Cases for appraisal and title search that must complete before closing. Which scenario represents the BEST fit for using a case-dependency Wait Step?

options.text: A loan parent Case must wait for its appraisal and title child Cases to be resolved before closing
A Case should pause until 9 AM tomorrow
A Case needs a duplicate search
A Case should route to a specific user

practiceQuiz.hint: Waiting on one or more related Cases to reach a status is the case-dependency Wait's specific purpose.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Waiting for child Cases (appraisal, title) to resolve before proceeding is a case-dependency Wait. The 9 AM scenario is a timer Wait; the others are different features.

optionExplanations.A: The parent depends on the resolved states of both children.
optionExplanations.B: A timestamp pause uses a timer rather than status dependency.
optionExplanations.C: Duplicate matching is a different workflow purpose.
optionExplanations.D: User routing is assignment allocation rather than dependency waiting.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is presenting the value of duplicate Case detection to a client operations manager who processes thousands of requests weekly. What is the main operational reason organizations implement duplicate Case detection?

options.text: It saves time and money by identifying and resolving duplicate work
It increases the number of Cases created
It replaces the need for SLAs
It eliminates parent/child relationships

practiceQuiz.hint: Detecting duplicate Cases before processing them avoids redundant work and wasted resources.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Detecting and resolving duplicate Cases avoids processing the same request twice, saving time and money. It does not increase Case volumes, replace SLAs, or alter parent/child relationships.

optionExplanations.A: Identifying redundant work avoids repeated processing effort.
optionExplanations.B: The goal is to reduce unnecessary work rather than create more.
optionExplanations.C: Valid work still needs deadline management.
optionExplanations.D: Hierarchical case design is independent of duplicate detection.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After a Case is resolved as Resolved-Duplicate, what can the workflow be customized to let the user do?

options.text: Open the original Case to make any necessary updates
Permanently lock all Rulesets
Create ten more duplicates automatically
Delete the original Case

practiceQuiz.hint: When a potential duplicate is found, the workflow should continue with only the genuine, original Case.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Processing can be customized so the user opens the original Case to update it, then continues with that genuine Case. The other options are incorrect.

optionExplanations.A: An original-case link lets the user continue valid work.
optionExplanations.B: Ruleset locking does not support the user's follow-up action.
optionExplanations.C: Producing more duplicates defeats the detection purpose.
optionExplanations.D: The original case holds the work that should continue.

quickRecap.value: Decompose complex work into focused, modular Case Types that work together; child Cases enable parallelism, specialization, independent SLAs, and reuse.
Case Dependency requires existing hierarchical children with any/all and target-status choices; Timer waits for a duration/timestamp. Resolved does not imply successful completion.
Search duplicate Cases Step compares property values using basic conditions (must match) + weighted conditions (summed vs. a threshold).
DOB (basic) + 4 weighted @25 each, threshold 50; full match = 100 ≥ 50 → flagged duplicate.
Confirmed duplicate → Resolved-Duplicate status (processing ends); optionally open the original Case to update it.
